blocks.text: CALASIAO, Pangasinan — Bangus (milkfish) producers must brace for the worsening effects of a projected super El Niño, which could severely affect aquaculture, a fisheries industry official said. Aquaculture operators have been adopting measures like deepening fishponds and using solar-powered equipment and other modern technologies to minimize the impact of prolonged hot and dry weather, said Wilfredo Cruz, Central Luzon director of the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), on the sidelines of the Third Bangus Congress, held on Oct. 14-16 at Clark in Pampanga. “An increase in pond water temperature causes cultured fish to eat less and affects their […]...
